title: Failure Modes of Vision-Language Models for Human Activity Understanding in Thermal HRI

problem.summary: Thermal cameras enable robots to perceive human activities in darkness while revealing less personally identifiable appearance information and fewer details of the surrounding environment than RGB cameras.
statements: Thermal cameras enable robots to perceive human activities in darkness while revealing less personally identifiable appearance information and fewer details of the surrounding environment than RGB cameras.

As vision-language models (VLMs), originally developed for RGB imagery, are increasingly integrated into embodied systems for scene understanding and high-level planning, thermal sensing offers a promising way to extend activity perception to low-light and privacy-sensitive settings.
However, the failure modes of VLMs in thermal human activity understanding for human-robot interaction (HRI) remain underexplored.

All models are served locally with vLLM on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU; models in the 30B range run from NVFP4-quantized checkpoints, while the smaller models run at native precision.
